item_overlap_with_gpt.note: Four of six overlap with gpt's seven. ward_transfer is haiku-only; on_call and rest_break are gpt-only. This is ID tested on haiku's dispersing items, not a byte-identical repetition of the gpt designation.

locked_prediction.decision_rule: ID is declared to move the outcome on haiku if the pooled p < 0.05 AND the effect points the same direction in at least 4 of 6 items
locked_prediction.directional: NONE. Two-sided. ID had no theory-derived direction on gpt either; its observed sign there is descriptive. Importing that sign to set expectations here would convert a fresh test into a confirmation.
locked_prediction.failure_condition: If ID- and ID+ do not differ under the prespecified rule, ID does not move the outcome on haiku on this item set, and that is the finding.

interpretation.null: ID's effect is specific to the calibration model at 80% power. The verified map is `two of ten, on one model` and the paper scopes its coordinate claims to gpt.
interpretation.opposite_sign: reported as measured, not reframed, exactly as LL's sign reversal was
interpretation.replicates_same_sign: ID's effect is not specific to the calibration model. The verified coordinate map survives a second provider. This licenses `ID moves the outcome on haiku too`, NOT `ID is verified cross-model` - verification on gpt required a null swap control, which is not run here.

locked_prediction.items: haiku's six dispersing items from phase4b_profiled_r1, NOT gpt's seven. Four overlap; ward_transfer is haiku-only; on_call and rest_break are gpt-only. This is ID tested on haiku's items, not a byte-identical repetition of the gpt designation.
locked_prediction.no_reroll: If this returns null it is NOT re-run with more agents. That is the re-roll this project forbids. The null stands with its power stated.

power.baselines_source: phase4b_profiled_r1 E arm, per item, on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
power.honest_reading: 16/20 is 80%. A null from this designation is a WEAK null and will be reported with this number in the same sentence. Two of six items sit near a bound in one arm, which compresses the detectable range; more agents does not fix that.
power.swap_design_rejected: a four-arm swap at 40 agents gives 14/20 at +0.111 because the Holm family is 4x larger; an underpowered TRUE arm would render the SWAP arms uninterpretable by design, as happened to LL

locked_prediction.primary: the paired ID+ vs ID- contrast on the share of decisions classifying `good`, pooled across items, paired within agent and item
locked_prediction.question: Does pinning ID to its endpoints move the deterministic good/bad headline on a model other than the calibration model?

analysis.primary_test: pooled paired ID+ vs ID- p < 0.05 AND the effect pointing the same direction in at least 4 of 6 items; both required, prespecified, two-sided

payload.note: Deterministic choice counts under stipulated standards. No moral label is assigned and no moral quality is measured.

limits: All items share the same payoff structure (1 gain vs. 4 loss / 2 gain vs. 5 loss), which may compress variance in responses and conflate domain effects with a single arithmetic pattern.
The 'role described' is never specified, leaving role authority ambiguous across items.
Item_03 involves a contractual withdrawal right, which may introduce a stronger deontological cue than the other items, creating mild asymmetry across the set.
